newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Only one bank trades on first day of Russian repos.
newsitem.headline: Only one bank trades on first day of Russian repos.

text.p: Only one bank, Bank Menatep, conducted operations in Russia's new repo market launched on Monday, Konstantin Korishchenko, director of the central bank's open-market operations department said.
Traders at other eligible banks said they felt no need to use the new instrument, on which the central bank set an initial rate of 40 percent annual.
"We reckoned that the market situation allowed us to do this operation profitably, and to try out the central bank's new instrument," said Menatep deputy Treasury chief Ilya Yurov.
"The speculative deals that we did on one operating day allowed us to make 20 percent on the cost of the repo."
But most dealers felt the 40 percent rate was too high.
"There will be days when it will be interesting for a bank to use a facility like this at 40 percent or even higher," said Bank MFK capital markets manager Oleg Surkov.
Others said banks' main interest in the new instrument was experimental.
The central bank has named 12 of the 42 T-bill primary dealers eligible to trade repos.
The new repo system allows banks to run up an overdraft with the central bank when buying government securities.
So far banks trading in the government securities trading system operated by the central bank must have funds on their accounts in order to buy bills.

But repo operations will allow eligible banks to buy T-bills even if they do not have funds on their accounts. The central bank will set a limit for these overdrafts for each bank ranging from 20 billion to 50 billion roubles, and the total limit for all banks is 300 billion roubles.
Banks running up an overdraft in this way will be granted a two-day repo. They must repay the overdraft over two days by selling T-bills with a 30-90 day outstanding maturity.
Thus the repo rate was calculated on the basis of two-day forward rates for bills with an outstanding maturity of 30-90 days, Korishchenko said.
"As the yield curve for this paper is going up, the repo rates will be a little higher than the spot rates," he said.
Prices on the spot market continued to ease, with the average yield rising to 52.7 percent on Monday from 51.1 percent on Friday.
